user_guidance.purpose: ROBERT curates tabular data, generates and validates machine-learning models, predicts values, and assembles reports.
when_to_use: Use ROBERT when the training table has molecular descriptors and a target property to model.
prerequisites: Provide descriptors and a target; ROBERT does not use raw structures by themselves as model features.
steps: Load the main CSV, choose the target and prediction type, select a workflow, and run ROBERT.
user_guidance.result: The selected ROBERT stages create model, validation, prediction, and report outputs appropriate to the workflow.
next_steps: Inspect Results > Report and validation evidence before using the model for new predictions.
common_issues: If the input contains only raw structures or SMILES, use optional AQME descriptor generation first.

records.title: ROBERT Full Workflow
question_patterns: how do I run all ROBERT stages

user_guidance.purpose: Run CURATE, GENERATE, VERIFY, PREDICT, and REPORT in sequence from the configured main CSV.
when_to_use: Use Full Workflow for a new end-to-end model run when the required training configuration is ready.
prerequisites: Load the main CSV and select the target column, prediction type, and Full Workflow.
steps: Review the configuration.
Choose Full Workflow in the workflow selector.
Press Run ROBERT and follow progress in the console.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT passes curated data into model generation, verifies selected models, produces applicable predictions, and builds the report.
next_steps: Open Results > Report and Images; open Predictions when matching prediction CSVs are available.
common_issues: A test CSV is optional for model training, and AQME is needed only when descriptors must be derived from structures.

records.title: Predict an external test CSV
question_patterns: how do I predict new molecules

user_guidance.purpose: Apply an existing trained ROBERT model to an external test CSV and create prediction outputs.
when_to_use: The test CSV is optional during training but required when you want external predictions for new candidates.
prerequisites: Keep the trained model outputs available and provide a test CSV with compatible descriptors, or compatible SMILES when the model used AQME.
steps: Select the Test CSV.
Choose PREDICT.
Press Run ROBERT and choose the descriptor strategy that matches model training.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT writes predictions for compatible rows and enables Results > Predictions when matching files are found.
next_steps: Inspect predicted values and uncertainty in Predictions, then compare them with the model report.
common_issues: Prediction fails when required descriptors differ from training or the existing GENERATE model folder cannot be found.

user_guidance.purpose: Check, clean, and filter the input table before model generation so unsuitable values and descriptors do not pass forward unnoticed.
when_to_use: Use CURATE before GENERATE for a new or changed training dataset.
prerequisites: Load a CSV and identify the target, name, ignored, and excluded columns correctly.
steps: Review column roles and run CURATE alone or as the first Full Workflow stage.
user_guidance.result: CURATE creates a prepared dataset that becomes the input to GENERATE.
next_steps: Run GENERATE on the curated output.
common_issues: Do not treat identifiers, comments, or structure strings as model descriptors unless they were intentionally encoded.

user_guidance.purpose: Explore model and descriptor combinations, tune candidates, and select promising models from curated data.
when_to_use: Use GENERATE after CURATE when you need to train or retrain models.
prerequisites: A curated dataset with a valid target and enough usable descriptor columns.
steps: Run GENERATE alone on an existing curated table or let Full Workflow call it after CURATE.
user_guidance.result: GENERATE stores candidate results and selected models, including variants with and without PFI descriptor reduction.
next_steps: Run VERIFY because model selection does not replace independent robustness checks.
common_issues: Very small, inconsistent, or descriptor-poor datasets can make model comparison unreliable.

records.title: VERIFY module
question_patterns: can I trust this ROBERT model

user_guidance.purpose: Apply robustness checks to selected models and expose warnings that affect confidence in their predictions.
when_to_use: Use VERIFY after GENERATE and before relying on a selected model.
prerequisites: A completed GENERATE stage with selected model files.
steps: Run VERIFY or let Full Workflow run it, then inspect every warning and validation plot.
user_guidance.result: VERIFY adds robustness evidence and warning results to the workflow outputs and report context.
next_steps: Interpret validation together with error metrics, applicability, and the final report.
common_issues: A strong training score does not override failed robustness checks or suspicious validation behavior.

user_guidance.purpose: Apply trained ROBERT models to compatible external data and create prediction tables and supporting diagnostics.
when_to_use: Use PREDICT when a trained model exists and new rows need estimated target values.
prerequisites: Provide the test CSV and the same descriptor information or AQME-compatible structures used by training.
steps: Select PREDICT, load the test CSV, run ROBERT, and answer the descriptor-strategy prompt consistently with training.
user_guidance.result: Prediction files are written and the Results > Predictions view becomes available when matching files are discovered.
next_steps: Review uncertainty, extrapolation, and the original validation before acting on predictions.
common_issues: Missing trained-model files or mismatched descriptor columns stop prediction rather than silently substituting features.

user_guidance.purpose: Assemble the PDF report and interpretation from model, validation, prediction, and diagnostic outputs.
when_to_use: Use REPORT after the relevant workflow stages have produced results, or rerun it to rebuild the summary.
prerequisites: Keep the workflow output folders and selected model results available.
steps: Run REPORT or complete Full Workflow, then open Results > Report and select Best models or a named model.
user_guidance.result: With all_models enabled, REPORT archives each generated model and variant PDF in REPORT_models and keeps one overall-best PDF in the run folder. With all_models disabled, REPORT writes separate No PFI and PFI PDFs for the selected model when PFI filtering is enabled; it writes only No PFI when PFI filtering is disabled or EVALUATE is used.
next_steps: Compare the available variant reports and read validation evidence rather than selecting a model from one metric.
common_issues: REPORT cannot reconstruct missing evidence. An N/A score can result from non-standard validation settings such as a single repeated CV run; it does not mean predictions or metric values are absent. REPORT's single overall-best PDF can differ from GENERATE's per-variant Best_model selections.

user_guidance.purpose: Identify the measured value that ROBERT should learn to predict from descriptor columns.
when_to_use: Choose it after loading the main CSV and before running any modelling workflow that needs a response.
prerequisites: The target column must contain the intended experimental or categorical outcome, not SMILES or an identifier.
steps: Select the correct column in Select Target Column (y), then choose the matching prediction type.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT uses this column as y during curation, training, validation, and reporting.
next_steps: Confirm whether its values represent regression or classification.
common_issues: Selecting a structure, name, or metadata column produces a model for the wrong task.

user_guidance.purpose: Tell ROBERT whether the target is a continuous value for regression or a category for classification.
when_to_use: Set Prediction Type for every model run and keep it consistent with the scientific question.
prerequisites: Inspect the target values and decide whether numerical distance or class membership is meaningful.
steps: Choose Regression for continuous quantities or Classification for discrete labels.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT selects task-appropriate models, scores, validation, and output interpretation.
next_steps: Review the workflow and run ROBERT.
common_issues: Numeric-looking class labels do not automatically make a task regression.

records.title: ROBERT report
question_patterns: how do I read the ROBERT report

user_guidance.purpose: Present model performance, validation tests, outlier and extrapolation evidence, and available predictions in a separate PDF for each available No PFI or PFI variant.
when_to_use: Read the report after a completed ROBERT workflow and before deciding whether a model is fit for use.
prerequisites: A generated ROBERT report PDF and the scientific context needed to judge the errors.
steps: Identify the model and No PFI or PFI variant in Results before interpreting the PDF.
Review metrics from the matching PREDICT_<model>_data.dat and VERIFY_<model>_data.dat files, validation warnings, outliers, applicability, and predictions together.
user_guidance.result: Each variant report provides Interpolation and, for regression, Boundary robustness scores alongside the evidence needed to interpret them.
next_steps: Investigate warnings or data limitations before making new predictions.
common_issues: Do not treat a visually prominent score as proof that all validation checks passed. Under all_models, compare model-specific DAT values and PDFs; a score marked N/A is unavailable rather than zero.

user_guidance.purpose: Summarize regression error in target units while giving larger errors extra weight through squaring.
when_to_use: Compare RMSE across models evaluated on comparable data and the same target scale.
prerequisites: Know the target units, data spread, split, and validation procedure.
steps: Read RMSE beside MAE, residual behavior, validation, and applicability evidence.
user_guidance.result: Lower comparable RMSE indicates smaller squared-error magnitude, but there is no universal cutoff for a good model.
next_steps: Inspect unusually large errors and validation warnings in the report.
common_issues: RMSE values from different targets, units, or data splits are not directly comparable.

user_guidance.purpose: Describe the average absolute prediction error in the same units as a continuous target.
when_to_use: Use MAE to communicate typical error magnitude on a comparable validation or test set.
prerequisites: Know the target units and how the evaluated rows were selected.
steps: Compare MAE with RMSE, residual plots, validation checks, and scientific tolerance.
user_guidance.result: Lower comparable MAE means smaller average absolute errors, but there is no universal cutoff independent of the problem.
next_steps: Use the report to inspect where errors occur and whether they are acceptable for the intended use.
common_issues: A modest average can hide important outliers, subgroups, or extrapolating predictions.

user_guidance.purpose: Describe how much target variation a regression model explains relative to a constant baseline on the evaluated data.
when_to_use: Use R2 as one contextual score for comparable regression evaluations, not as a standalone approval rule.
prerequisites: Check the evaluated split, target range, sample count, and error magnitudes.
steps: Interpret R2 with RMSE, MAE, residuals, validation tests, and the report.
user_guidance.result: A higher comparable R2 may indicate better explained variation, but no single cutoff guarantees useful predictions.
next_steps: Confirm that absolute errors and validation behavior meet the scientific need.
common_issues: A high R2 can coexist with large errors, leakage, narrow target ranges, or weak extrapolation.

records.title: Permutation feature importance (PFI)
question_patterns: why are there PFI and no PFI models

user_guidance.purpose: Estimate descriptor importance by measuring how model performance changes when each feature is shuffled.
when_to_use: Use PFI results to compare a reduced descriptor model with the corresponding no-PFI model.
prerequisites: A generated model and a consistent evaluation procedure.
steps: Compare PFI and no-PFI performance, retained descriptors, validation, and report evidence.
user_guidance.result: PFI can produce a simpler descriptor set, but there is no universal cutoff that makes a retained feature scientifically causal.
next_steps: Check whether the reduced model remains robust and appropriate for prediction.
common_issues: Correlated descriptors can share importance, and importance does not by itself prove mechanism or causation.

records.title: ROBERT run prerequisites
question_patterns: what is required before Run ROBERT
what do I need before running ROBERT

user_guidance.purpose: Identify the required and conditional setup before a ROBERT job can start safely.
when_to_use: Check the main CSV, target, prediction type, and workflow when Run ROBERT is blocked or a preflight popup reports missing input.
prerequisites: The main CSV, target, prediction type, and workflow are required for model-building runs.
steps: Load the main CSV.
Select the target and task type.
Select the workflow.
Add a test CSV only for external prediction and enable AQME only when descriptors must be generated.
user_guidance.result: A complete configuration lets ROBERT build the intended command and start the selected workflow.
next_steps: Run ROBERT and monitor the popup plus console for the next concrete issue.
common_issues: A test CSV is conditional, AQME is conditional, and PREDICT additionally needs compatible data plus an existing trained model.
